cards.text: We're back in Jerusalem, where King David has gathered all the leaders of Israel. He's just handed his son Solomon the plans for the LORD's temple. Now David turns to the whole assembly and talks about his boy.

cards.question: David tells the assembly that Solomon, the one God has chosen, is young and ___.
David tells the assembly that the task ahead of Solomon is great. What reason does he give?

answers.text: The palace is for the LORD God
The land is full of enemies

cards.text: With all his ability, David has already stockpiled gold, silver, bronze, iron, wood, precious stones and slabs of marble, all in abundance. Friend, I get excited when I find a second bag of chocolate chips in the back of the cupboard.
But David's not done. Over and above all that, he's got one more thing to give.

cards.question: Over and above what he's already provided, David gives his ___ treasures of gold and silver for the temple.
Why does David give his own gold and silver for the temple?

answers.text: His delight in the house of his God
Nathan the prophet told him to

cards.text: Three thousand talents of gold, the gold of Ophir, plus seven thousand talents of refined silver to overlay the walls. Baker, the most gold I've ever owned is this base I'm standing on, and I didn't even BUY it.

cards.question: After giving his own gold and silver, David turns to the assembly with a question. What does he ask?

answers.text: Who is willing to consecrate himself to the LORD today
Who will march out against the Philistines with me
Who will go up to Lebanon to cut cedar

cards.text: Then the leaders step up: heads of families, officers of the tribes, commanders of thousands and of hundreds, and the officials over the king's work.

cards.question: True or false: the leaders give only because King David orders them to.

cards.text: Their gifts pile up: thousands of talents of gold, silver and bronze, and 100,000 talents of iron. ONE HUNDRED THOUSAND, friend, somebody go check if the floor's holding.
And whoever has precious stones brings them to the treasury of the LORD's house.

cards.question: Who looks after the treasury where the precious stones go?
The leaders have given to the LORD freely and wholeheartedly, and the people ___ at their willing response.
True or false: King David rejoices greatly too.

cards.text: Then David blesses the LORD right in front of the whole assembly. He starts BIG: "May You be blessed, O LORD, God of our father Israel, from everlasting to everlasting."
David says what belongs to the LORD: the greatness, the power, the glory, the splendor and the majesty. The kingdom too.

cards.question: In his prayer, David says the greatness, the power and the glory belong to the LORD. What reason does he give?

answers.text: Everything in heaven and on earth is His
He won every battle for Israel
His temple will be the greatest one

cards.text: Then David brings up riches and honor. Friend, there's a MOUNTAIN of riches sitting right in front of this crowd.

cards.question: In his prayer, David says riches and honor come from ___.

cards.text: So David says, "Now therefore, our God, we give You thanks, and we praise Your glorious name."

Then David asks, "But who am I, and who are my people, that we should be able to give as generously as this?" Baker, I started out in a clearance bin with a 25-cent sticker on me, so I ask that question EVERY morning.

cards.question: David asks how he and his people could give so generously. What answer does he give God?

answers.text: Everything comes from God's own hand
The people worked extra hard all year
The king of Tyre sent them help

cards.text: Then David gets humble: "For we are foreigners and strangers in Your presence, as were all our forefathers. Our days on earth are like a shadow, without hope."

cards.question: True or false: David tells God that all the abundance provided for the temple belongs to the people who gave it.
In his prayer, David says God delights in uprightness. What does David say God tests?
True or false: David tells God he gave all his gifts willingly and with an upright heart.

cards.text: Now David calls on the LORD, God of Abraham, Isaac and Israel. He's got a request for the people standing around him.

cards.question: What does David ask the LORD to keep forever in His people's hearts?

answers.text: The same desire they just showed

cards.question: David asks God to give his son Solomon a ___ heart to keep all His commandments and build His palace.

cards.text: Prayer's done. David turns to the whole assembly and says, "Bless the LORD your God."

cards.question: True or false: the whole assembly blesses the LORD, and they bow down and pay homage to the LORD and to the king.

cards.text: The next day, they bring sacrifices and burnt offerings to the LORD: a thousand bulls, a thousand rams and a thousand lambs, plus drink offerings. Friend, my biggest batch ever was six dozen cookies, and I had to sit down on my base afterward.
That day, they eat and drink with great joy in the presence of the LORD.

cards.question: For a second time, the people do something for David's son Solomon. What do they do?
Along with Solomon, ___ is anointed as the priest.

cards.text: So Solomon sits on the throne of the LORD as king, in place of his father David.

cards.question: Solomon is now on the throne. How does his reign begin?

answers.text: He prospers and all Israel obeys him
The tribes rise up against him

cards.question: True or false: some of King David's sons refuse to pledge their allegiance to King Solomon.

cards.text: Then the LORD highly exalts Solomon in the sight of all Israel.

cards.question: True or false: no king in Israel before Solomon was given royal majesty like the LORD gives Solomon.

cards.text: Now the book looks back. David son of Jesse was king over all Israel, and he reigned forty years.

cards.question: David reigned seven years in ___ and thirty-three years in ___.
After forty years as king, how does David's life end?

answers.text: He dies at a ripe old age full of honor
He falls in battle against the Philistines
He dies alone and forgotten in the palace

cards.text: Everything King David did, first to last, is written in the Chronicles of Samuel the Seer, Nathan the Prophet and Gad the Seer. Forty years of David, and friend, it took THREE of them to keep up.

findings.problem: The card states facts from the previous passage: David gathered all the leaders of Israel in Jerusalem (1 Chronicles 28:1) and just handed Solomon the temple plans (1 Chronicles 28:11). It cites only 1 Chronicles 29:1 and gives no reference for those facts.

rule.text: Facts from outside the passage are fine when they help, like who a new person is or who wrote a letter, with their reference.

findings.problem: The question asks who looks after the treasury (Jehiel the Gershonite). That is a minor detail that doesn't move the passage forward or help the baker understand it, and it can only be guessed by luck. The moment of the precious stones being given is already told on card 13.

rule.text: Ask about the moments that move the passage forward and the details the baker needs to understand it.

findings.problem: "There's a MOUNTAIN of riches sitting right in front of this crowd" is stated as fact, not as a joke. The text never says the gifts are piled up in front of the assembly (verse 8 puts the stones in the treasury). The line also reads as a plain remark rather than a laugh.

rule.text: Don't stretch the text. Exaggerate only in his own jokes.

findings.problem: The card cites 1 Chronicles 29:29-30 but only tells verse 29, which covers King David's acts from first to last and the three chronicles. Verse 30 (the details of his reign, his might, and the circumstances that came on him, Israel and all the kingdoms) isn't told. Either narrow the citation or tell verse 30.

rule.text: Every story card cites the verses it tells, from the first verse it uses to the last, no wider and no narrower.
